column1: # The converter's rules for the hand-written adapters of the step down to 1.20.4 (top-version names; tabs).
# P <class>                                   a class the adapters provide (in place of carrying it)
# N <class>                                   new above although its intermediary twin exists below (another class)
#                                             an override of a newer method: the mod class gets the interface (the
#                                             adapters' mixins call it from 1.20.4's call sites); a super call into the
#                                             game's own class goes to the defaults method (receiver first)
#                                             a call goes to the adapter's static method (receiver first)
# R <class> <lower class>                     a class renamed below with the same members (NeoForge has no intermediary)
#                                             a field the adapters give: its reads go to the getter (an instance
#                                             a constructor that takes more below (new X(..) and super(..)): each
#                                             lower parameter is an upper one ($0, $1..) or an adapter method's value,
#                                             the method given all the upper arguments; ladder/bottom/<class> names
#                                             the bottom class a top class of the same name hides
#                                             the same hook (of the owner and its subclasses) under another name and
#                                             descriptor below; the generated bridges take it from there
# NeoForge 20.5's tick events: posted from 1.20.4's TickEvent by the adapters (ladder.adapter.event.TickBridge)
# NeoForge 21.0 renamed tool actions to item abilities
# small members of the newer versions
# FML 4 extension points: the config screen factory as 1.20.4
# 1.21's vertex API: buffers begun by the tesselator, built into MeshData, vertices ended by the next one
# the setters gather the begun vertex's attributes (1.21 takes them in any order; 1.20.4 in its format's)
# DFU 8 (1.21) on DFU 6 (1.20.4): new members, and two changes the descriptors hide (dispatch types give map codecs; errors are Errors)
# 1.21's DeltaTracker (the frame's time): the client's own from 1.20.4's timer; a partial tick where 1.20.4 passes one
# more small members of 1.20.5: a tooltip's context, a state's pathfinding and use, a spawn's NBT, the component serializer's registries
# 1.20.5's block entity load and save entries
# 1.20.5 split BlockEntity.load into loadAdditional (the per-class hook, registries passed) and loadWithComponents
# Data components (the first compatibility module): types, the registry, a stack's values kept in its NBT
# network: 1.20.5's static FriendlyByteBuf helpers on any ByteBuf (ByteBufCodecs and the STREAM_CODECs need them)
# network: what ByteBufCodecs and the payloads need of classes 1.20.4 has (new members, new STREAM_CODEC fields)
# network: 1.20.5 payloads on 20.4 (registration, the handler context, sending; items, ingredients and text as stream codecs)
# network: FriendlyByteBuf helpers that take stream codecs since 1.20.5 (1.20.4: Reader / Writer functions)
# classes whose intermediary twin below is another class
# armour: 1.20.5's ArmorMaterial is a record in a registry (1.20.4: an interface the ArmorMaterials enum implements)
# recipes: 1.21 recipe serializers give a stream codec (1.20.4: fromNetwork / toNetwork)
# 1.20.5 item stack codecs beside the component ones (strict: stack size checked; single item: {id, components})
# recipes: getRecipeFor with the last recipe (1.20.4 gives a pair), stream codecs 1.20.4 has as toNetwork / fromNetwork
# NeoForge 20.5's custom ingredients (ICustomIngredient, carried) as 20.4 ingredients; their types as 20.4's
